description: I'm a full-stack developer with expertise in React, Tailwind CSS, 3D visualization, and AI integration. Passionate about space tech and immersive web experiences, I'm building AstroMind AI to turn raw NASA datasets into an interactive, layered Marswalk navigation and analysis HUD. Looking for UI/UX designers, GIS/data specialists, researchers, and space enthusiasts!
summary: AstroMind AI is an interactive, map-based platform designed to help users explore and compare locations on Mars using scientific data from multiple space missions. It brings together Mars imagery, orbital terrain datasets, and atmospheric model layers in one workspace. Users can inspect geographic locations, explore available data layers, compare regions, and review exploratory Landing Suitability and Human Settlement Suitability indicators. The platform emphasizes scientific transparency by distinguishing direct observations, orbital datasets, model estimates, derived indicators, nearby mission references, and unavailable data. Rather than claiming that a location is safe for landing or human settlement, AstroMind AI helps users understand the available evidence, identify data gaps, and make more informed comparisons for future Mars exploration
details:
AstroMind AI is an interactive, map-centered platform designed to support the exploration and comparison of locations on Mars using scientific datasets from multiple Mars missions. It brings together planetary imagery, orbital elevation data, terrain information, thermal observations, and atmospheric model layers in one integrated workspace

Users can explore the Martian surface, navigate geographic locations, inspect available data layers, examine terrain characteristics, and compare selected regions. The platform also includes exploratory Landing Suitability Index (LSI) and Human Settlement Suitability Index (HSI) indicators to help organize available evidence and highlight factors relevant to future exploration

A key feature of AstroMind AI is its evidence-transparency approach. It distinguishes orbital observations, model estimates, derived products, nearby mission references, and unavailable data instead of presenting all information as equally certain. Missing datasets are not automatically treated as unfavorable conditions

The platform uses Mars datasets and resources including Viking MDIM imagery, MOLA elevation and slope data, THEMIS daytime infrared data, selected HiRISE and CTX imagery, and TES thermal inertia data. It also references Mars Climate Database model outputs where applicable

AstroMind AI was developed as a web-based application using AI-assisted development tools. The team used ChatGPT and Lovable to support development and refinement. The project aims to make complex Mars exploration data more accessible, encourage evidence-based site comparison, and provide a foundation for future improvements as additional datasets become available

The LSI and HSI indicators are exploratory tools, not validated assessments of landing safety or human habitability. Data coverage and resolution vary by dataset and location


AI-assisted tools, including ChatGPT and Lovable, were used during the development process to support brainstorming, research organization, technical planning, coding, debugging, and content refinement. The team reviewed and integrated the generated outputs. Scientific datasets and mission information were obtained from their respective sources rather than being treated as AI-generated facts. The project does not claim that its exploratory suitability indicators are validated AI predictions or official NASA assessments
